newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - U.S. T-bonds eye key 114-15 retracement.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - U.S. T-bonds eye key 114-15 retracement.

text.p: U.S. September Treasury bonds began the week firm, edging toward a key retracement level at 114-15/32.
Several technicians said market behavior on reaching that mark will dictate where September will go from here.

"That will be the deciding area," said Jim Hyerczyk, a technician with JAH Research and Trading. "I think the bond market the next two days is going to short-cover until (Federal Open Market Committee results Tuesday), and it's likely to rally back to 114-15/32." That level marks a 50 percent retracement of the 116-31/32 to 111-31/32 break.
At 1237 CDT/1737 GMT, September T-bonds were up 16/32 at 114-4/32 in a range from 113-21/32 to 114-11/32.
Hyerczyk said the market would either extend above the retracement to next resistance at 115-06/32, or begin a sell-off to 109-15/32.
Holly Liss, assistant vice president of technical analysis with Sakura Dellsher, agreed that the next short-term upside target is 114-13/32 to 15/32.
"It looks pretty constructive short-term," she said. She called 112-17/32 "major, major support," and said the market has been building a base since August 7.
"That support is moving up a tick a day, and you break that and you're definitely moving up to higher yields," Liss said.
Barring a break, next major upside resistance after the 50-percent retracement is 115-1/32 to 6/32, she said.

Still, several traders cautioned that the intermediate-term trend was still bearish for bonds. Floor traders said the market could be prone to nervousness ahead of Tuesday's FOMC results and after recent gains from the break to 111-31/32.
Jim Grauer, president of Omnitrage, said the time was ripe for a short down-cycle since the market filled in a 100-minute gap on Monday at 113-27/32 to 114-5/32.
Hyerczyk said weekly charts still showed bearish technicals for bonds.
"If we get a selloff at 114-15/32, then we'll probably break to 109-15/32," Hyerczyk warned, adding that a close above 115-6/32 was needed "to turn the trend back up."
